design: Flying MicroDuck four-EDF jetpack, printed parts: a wing plate between the OpenRB rear pack and the battery backpack on the four existing post holes (shared M2 x 10 screws), two battery trays, two nacelles (inner and outer clamp halves around two ARESWEI HDS001 50 mm EDFs each, ears captured at the split), FC/ESC bracket on the right arm with the flow-module shelf under it at the right rear. No compass part: the external GPS/compass module is deleted. Frame: guide frame, mm (x forward, y left, z up); stand-keyframe world z = guide z + 120.

approved.history: 2026-11-10 (docs/PET_ROBOT_LOG.md): four 50 mm EDFs on 4S chosen over 64 mm; thrust taken as the vendor figure (no bench gate); the wing plate must not block the A7Z rear ports or rest on the taped saddle; the Dual Lock back plate is not fitted, the battery backpack sits directly on the OpenRB box; Shawn chose shared screws: backpack front plate 2 mm + wing-plate centre 3.5 mm + M2 x 10 (4.5 mm bite in the 4.8 mm pilots). The fans are NOT in hand (nothing ordered); Shawn asked for slice files now, so every fan-dependent dimension is a parameter in cad/flight_params.py FAN, fed from the maker drawing the coordinator read (QX-Motor 50 mm 12-blade: lip OD 63.0, duct OD 54.0, housing 39.08, motor OD 25.8 printed; the rest scaled +-0.4 mm). Fan reference: lip-face centres at x +20 and -44, y +-110, lip top at guide z 75 (stand 195), duct axes canted 6 deg fore-aft (front fans' exhaust forward, rear fans' rearward). Later on 2026-11-10 Shawn deleted the external GPS/compass module from the cart ('删掉', relayed by the coordinator): heading comes from the duck's own IMU via the A7Z (ArduPilot ExternalNav yaw) with the FC's onboard compass as fallback, so no compass bracket is printed. The XT60 pigtails left the cart too (RoboClub stock); the battery-lead routing is unchanged. Fan change, 2026-11-10 (relayed by the coordinator): Shawn took the fans from Amazon instead of qwinout, 'can do, I have added 4, you can clear it for me' (quote above): four ARESWEI HDS001 50 mm 11-blade 4650KV (2 CW, 2 CCW), delivery shown 2026-11-12, replacing the QX-Motor 50 mm 12-blade. The fan is the parameter set ARESWEI_HDS001 in cad/flight_params.py (FANS); the QX set stays as a second set. Shawn rejected a caliper sheet the same day (quote above): fan dimensions come from the listing drawing, no caliper step. The stated values (overall 3.3 in, inlet lip 2.3 in, rear ring 2.0 in, housing 1.3 in, motor 0.9 in, each rounded to 0.1 in, so +-1.3 mm) and the pixel reads scaled from them set the parameters, and the nacelle is built to fit the whole band: a split gap that closes under the clamp screws plus one layer of 1 mm foam tape in each bore, axial stops and ear pockets with +-1.5 mm clearance, lead slots for every lead direction the moulding allows. Fan reference positions (lip-face centres, lip top z 75, 6 deg cant) are unchanged. Post screws, 2026-11-10 (relayed by the coordinator, quote '用 M2×12'): to deepen the wing-plate root band to 8.5 mm (strength check, plain PLA), the battery backpack moves 3.4 mm further back and the wing-plate centre grows from 3.5 to 6.9 mm; the four shared post screws become M2 x 12 from the Zuorery M2 kit on Shawn's bench (backpack front plate 2 mm + wing centre 6.9 mm + 3.1 mm bite in the 4.8 mm deep post pilots). This replaces the M2 x 10 stack for these four screws only; the backpack still sits directly on the OpenRB box, the back plate is still not fitted, and the wing plate still shares the four post screws.
